$comment: DERIVED, not verbatim. Written by this library from the prose of the W3C Recommendation Verifiable Credential Data Integrity 1.0 (REC-vc-data-integrity-20250515), which prints no JSON Schema, CDDL or ABNF of its own (README.md gives the search). Source .cache/w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0.bin, sha256 ba5c4baf13fe3bab3ebd95ab6650d6fe83720e254b383bb444b4fbbae7bcf4fe; quotations are cut from its rendering .cache/w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0.txt, sha256 2b7725f80e138ef943eff25050eee6a62f8887762ca9e1e03867c55ea5647beb, and cite its line numbers (L). LEVELS: the root and every anchor not ending in -should state MUST and MUST NOT rules, so a failure there is non-conformance; an anchor ending in -should adds SHOULD statements and includes the root by reference, so a failure there is a warning. MAY statements are never constraints: a leniency a MAY grants has its own anchor, named for the leniency. A constraint marked INFERRED is a reading this library made, not a statement of the source; one marked OUTSIDE-SOURCE comes from a document the source names and is not this source's. Rule ids (P-nn, S-nn, V-nn, E-nn, O-nn, M-nn) are those of rules.derived.yaml. INSTANCE: one data integrity proof object, the value of the proof property of a secured document (section 2.1), as a JSON object. ROOT = section 2.1 MUST rules for a proof (strict time values). ANCHORS: #data-integrity-proof (section 3.1 MUST rules), #processable (the verificationMethod the Add Proof and Verify Proof algorithms need, though section 2.1 makes it OPTIONAL: a source tension, README T-01), #lenient-time (the MAY of section 2.1 to consume time values with no offset), #url-strict (INFERRED: id, verificationMethod and previousProof as absolute URLs), #multibase-base58btc and #multibase-base64url (OUTSIDE-SOURCE: Multibase prefixes z and u, which this source does not name; its examples use z), #proof-should (SHOULD: a challenge when a domain is present). Properties the source does not list are allowed (w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0053): “and MAY define other properties specific to their cryptographic suite” (L524).
title: A data integrity proof object (DERIVED)

core.$comment: Everything in the root except the type of created and expires, which the root makes strict and #lenient-time makes lenient.

id.$comment: P-01 w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0003: “An optional identifier for the proof, which MUST be a URL [URL]” (L205). Optional. A URL as the WHATWG URL Standard defines one is approximated by a string that opens with a scheme and holds no whitespace; INFERRED: the source's own example is a urn:uuid, and a relative reference is dropped under a null base URL (w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0036).

type.$comment: P-02 w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0004: “The specific type of proof MUST be specified as a string that maps to a URL [URL].” (L207). Required, a string. A string that MAPS to a URL is a JSON-LD term or compact IRI as often as a URL, so no URL pattern is applied (DataIntegrityProof is the source's own example).

proofPurpose.$comment: P-03 w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0005: “The reason the proof was created MUST be specified as a string that maps to a URL [URL].” (L209). Required, a string. The commonly used values are listed in section 2.2 (I-02) and are not a closed set: “The following is a list of commonly used proof purpose values.” (L373)

verificationMethod.$comment: P-04 w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0006: “If included, the value MUST be a string that maps to a [URL].” (L211). A string when present. Optional here (w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0007: “Inclusion of verificationMethod is OPTIONAL” (L211)); #processable requires it.

cryptosuite.$comment: P-05 w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0009: “If specified, its value MUST be a string.” (L213). A string when present. When it is REQUIRED is the allOf rule below (w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0008).

domain.$comment: P-07 w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0015: “If specified, the associated value MUST be either a string, or an unordered set of strings.” (L219). A string, or an array of strings with no repeated member (an unordered set). The associated value may also be a single-element set written as a string; the two are equivalent for matching (w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0069).

challenge.$comment: P-08 w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0017: “A string value that SHOULD be included in a proof if a domain is specified.” (L221). The type is the definitional clause; no keyword and so no MUST. Its SHOULD is #proof-should.

proofValue.$comment: P-09 w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0018: “The value MUST use a header and encoding as described in Section 2.4 Multibase of the Controlled Identifiers v1.0 specification” (L223). A string whose first character is the Multibase header. Which headers exist is Controlled Identifiers v1.0 and Multibase's, not this source's; #multibase-base58btc and #multibase-base64url pin the two this lane was asked about. w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0019 lets a cryptosuite use other properties instead of proofValue, so proofValue is optional in the root and required in #data-integrity-proof.

previousProof.$comment: P-10 w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0019: “If present, it MUST be a string value or an unordered list of string values.” (L225). A string, or an array of strings; the source says list here and set for domain, so duplicates are not forbidden. That each value names a proof of the same document is cross-field rule X-01 (w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0020, w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0063, w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0072), which a JSON Schema cannot state.

nonce.$comment: P-11 w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0021: “An OPTIONAL string value supplied by the proof creator.” (L227). Optional, a string.

allOf.$comment: P-06 w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0008: “If the proof type is DataIntegrityProof, cryptosuite MUST be specified; otherwise, cryptosuite MAY be specified.” (L213). The if tests that type is present AND equal, because an if over properties alone is true when type is absent and would make the rule vacuous in the other direction.

created.$comment: P-12 w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0009: “if included, MUST be specified as an [XMLSCHEMA11-2] dateTimeStamp string, either in Universal Coordinated Time (UTC), denoted by a Z at the end of the value, or with a time zone offset relative to UTC.” (L215) The XSD 1.1 dateTimeStamp lexical form: a dateTime whose explicit time zone is required. The pattern checks the lexical form; it does not reject a day that the calendar lacks (2020-02-30T00:00:00Z) or a 24:00:00 that XSD maps to the next day: schema-tests.derived.json carries both as limitations.

expires.$comment: P-13 w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0012: “If present, it MUST be an [XMLSCHEMA11-2] dateTimeStamp string, either in Universal Coordinated Time (UTC), denoted by a Z at the end of the value, or with a time zone offset relative to UTC.” (L217) Same pattern as created. Optional (w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0011). The source states no ordering between created and expires, and none is enforced.

lenient.$comment: ANCHOR #lenient-time. Everything in the root, but created and expires also take a dateTime with no offset.

created.$comment: P-14 w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0010: “A conforming processor MAY chose to consume time values that were incorrectly serialized without an offset.” (L215) “Incorrectly serialized time values without an offset are to be interpreted as UTC.” (L215) (w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0011). A permission of a processor, so it is not in the root; a value without an offset is read as UTC.

expires.$comment: P-15 w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0013, w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0014: the same permission and reading for expires (L217).

type.$comment: P-16 w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0051: “The type property MUST contain the string DataIntegrityProof.” (L519)

cryptosuite.$comment: P-17 w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0051: “The value of the cryptosuite property MUST be a string that identifies the cryptographic suite.” (L521) Required here (w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0008). The subtype rule is w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0052: “If the processing environment supports string subtypes, the subtype of the cryptosuite value MUST be the https://w3id.org/security#cryptosuiteString subtype.” (L521) A JSON string has no subtype, so no JSON Schema keyword can state it.

proofValue.$comment: P-18 w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0052: “The proofValue property MUST be used, as specified in Section 2.1 Proofs.” (L523) Required here. This contradicts section 2.1, which lets a cryptosuite use alternative properties INSTEAD of proofValue (w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0019): README T-02.

processable.$comment: ANCHOR #processable. What Add Proof and Verify Proof need. P-19 w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0059: “If one or more of the proof.type, proof.verificationMethod, and proof.proofPurpose values is not set, an error MUST be raised and SHOULD convey an error type of PROOF_GENERATION_ERROR.” (L551) w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0067: “If one or more of proof.type, proof.verificationMethod, and proof.proofPurpose does not exist, an error MUST be raised and SHOULD convey an error type of PROOF_VERIFICATION_ERROR.” (L603) So a proof that Add Proof returns and Verify Proof accepts has verificationMethod, though section 2.1 makes it OPTIONAL (README T-01).

urlStrict.$comment: ANCHOR #url-strict. INFERRED: the identifiers of section 2.1 as absolute URLs. Basis: with no base URL, a relative reference is dropped, and dropping must be an error (w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0035, w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0036).

b58.$comment: ANCHOR #multibase-base58btc. OUTSIDE-SOURCE: Multibase header z, base58 bitcoin alphabet. Not named by this source; every proofValue in its examples is of this form.

b64u.$comment: ANCHOR #multibase-base64url. OUTSIDE-SOURCE: Multibase header u, base64url alphabet without padding. Not named by this source and not used in its examples.

proofShould.$comment: ANCHOR #proof-should. SHOULD level, includes the root. P-20 w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0017: “A string value that SHOULD be included in a proof if a domain is specified.” (L221) A deviation, not non-conformance. Two further SHOULDs are not shape rules: w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0016 (a verifier uses domain, L219) and w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0054 (new suites use the DataIntegrityProof pattern, L527).
